page: Google Cloud Platform h4d-highmem-192 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance from the h4d server family. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, paired with 1488.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per core, positioning it for memory-intensive enterprise workloads.

This instance type does not include local NVMe SSD storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The absence of local storage and hardware accelerators represents a design tradeoff, focusing resources entirely on high-capacity memory and compute density.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the h4d-highmem-192 offers a high density of dedicated compute cores and memory resources within a single virtualized boundary, reducing the overhead of managing multiple smaller instances. It is designed for large-scale workloads such as in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, large-scale data analytics, and memory-bound simulation tasks.
